title: Tech Note: Generic Full Data Export-Import Routine
author: Thomas Maul, General Manager, 4D Germany.
featured_technology: BLOB and picture field Base64 encoding
Data file defragmentation / index rebuild / sequence number restoration

historical_commentary.text: This note provides a single, self-contained 4D method that exports or imports an entire database (all tables, subtables, pictures, and BLOBs) to/from XML, intended for long-term archiving, disaster recovery, and defragmenting data files by round-tripping through a text export. The generic full-export/full-import-to-repair-data-file pattern remains a legitimate and still-used technique in 4D today, though the specific single-method implementation, its manual handling of table/field name sanitization, and the 1.5GB per-file segmentation workaround for older Mac OS file-size limits are dated relative to 4D's later built-in backup, XML, and data-file maintenance tooling.
related_updates: 4D has since expanded its native XML import/export commands and data file maintenance tools (compacting, verifying, and repairing structure/data files) beyond what was available in 4D 2004
The 1.5GB Mac OS file-size segmentation workaround described here reflects limitations of mid-2000s Mac OS file systems that no longer apply to modern systems
